lessons.title: Report architecture: सारांश, निष्कर्ष, सिफ़ारिश
lessons.learn: A Hindi report is read from the top and trusted from the bottom: सारांश (summary) first, then विधि/आधार, निष्कर्ष (findings), सिफ़ारिश (recommendation), and परिशिष्ट (annexure) for the evidence. The summary is written last and placed first, and it must be readable on its own — that is the whole test of the form.

grammar.title: Summary first, evidence last
grammar.explain: The architecture is fixed: सारांश → आधार → निष्कर्ष → सिफ़ारिश → परिशिष्ट. Each section opens with its own one-line statement — इस रिपोर्ट में … (this report …), निष्कर्ष यह है कि … (the finding is that …), सिफ़ारिश है कि … (the recommendation is that …). A report without सिफ़ारिश is a description, not a report.
grammar.pattern: इस रिपोर्ट में … · निष्कर्ष यह है कि … · सिफ़ारिश है कि …

examples.t: इस रिपोर्ट में तीन निष्कर्ष हैं।
examples.r: is riporṭ meṅ tīn niṣkarṣ haiṅ.
examples.en: This report has three findings.

examples.t: निष्कर्ष यह है कि माँग बढ़ रही है।
examples.r: niṣkarṣ yah hai ki māṅg baṛh rahī hai.
examples.en: The finding is that demand is growing.

examples.t: सिफ़ारिश है कि पहले आधा काम शुरू किया जाए।
examples.r: sifāriś hai ki pahle ādhā kām śurū kiyā jāe.
examples.en: The recommendation is that half the work be started first.

mistakes.wrong: रिपोर्ट में सब कुछ लिखा है, आप पढ़ लीजिए।
mistakes.right: सारांश पहले पेज पर है; निष्कर्ष और सिफ़ारिश अलग-अलग दिए हैं।
mistakes.why: a report nobody can enter is a report nobody reads. The summary is a service to the reader, and at C1+ the architecture is the writing.

dialogue.r: riporṭ kahāṅ tak pahuṅcī?
dialogue.en: How far has the report got?

dialogue.t: सारांश और निष्कर्ष तैयार हैं। सिफ़ारिश बाक़ी है।

dialogue.en: The summary and findings are ready. The recommendation is left.

dialogue.t: सिफ़ारिश के बिना रिपोर्ट अधूरी है।
dialogue.r: sifāriś ke binā riporṭ adhūrī hai.

dialogue.r: sahī bāt hai — kal tak do sifāriśeṅ joṛ dūṅgā.
dialogue.en: Fair point — I will add two recommendations by tomorrow.

lessons.title: Concise institutional prose
lessons.learn: Institutional Hindi becomes unreadable by piling up nouns: समस्त प्रकार की व्यवस्थाओं का यथाशीघ्र क्रियान्वयन किया जाएगा. The fix is a verb, a subject and fewer words: जल्दी लागू किया जाएगा. C1+ writing is judged on what has been removed — यथाशीघ्र, समस्त, प्रकार की, संबंधी are the usual four to cut.

grammar.title: Cut the noun pile, restore the verb
grammar.explain: Legalese stacks nouns and hides the verb at the end: व्यवस्थाओं का क्रियान्वयन किया जाएगा. Concise institutional Hindi puts the verb in plain sight and keeps the noun count low: जल्दी लागू किया जाएगा. The passive किया जाएगा is still right for an impersonal order — what changes is the weight in front of it, not the grammar.
grammar.pattern: … किया जाएगा · … जल्दी लागू होगा · संक्षिप्त कीजिए

examples.t: यह प्रक्रिया जल्दी लागू की जाएगी।

examples.en: This procedure will be implemented soon.

examples.r: anāvaśyak śabd haṭā dījie.
examples.en: Remove the unnecessary words.

examples.t: संक्षिप्त कीजिए — पाठक को समय चाहिए।

examples.en: Shorten it — the reader needs time.

mistakes.right: यह प्रक्रिया जल्दी लागू की जाएगी।
mistakes.why: समस्त, प्रकार की and यथाशीघ्र add no information and cost the reader a sentence. In institutional Hindi the shorter sentence is not less official — it is more enforceable.

lessons.title: Editing someone else's draft
lessons.learn: Editing in Hindi is a protocol as much as a skill: पहले पढ़ लीजिए, फिर बदलिए (read first, then change), सुझाव दीजिए, आदेश नहीं (suggest, do not order), and मूल भाव बना रहे (the original sense must survive). Say what a change buys: बदलाव से अर्थ साफ़ होगा.

grammar.title: सुझाव दीजिए, आदेश नहीं
grammar.explain: Comment on a draft with suggestions, not corrections: यहाँ बदलाव से अर्थ साफ़ होगा (a change here will make the meaning clear), शायद यह वाक्य छोटा किया जा सके (this sentence could perhaps be shortened). मूल भाव बना रहे is the constraint that governs every suggestion, and स्वर (tone) is what an edit most easily damages.
grammar.pattern: यहाँ बदलाव से … होगा · शायद … किया जा सके · मूल भाव बना रहे

examples.t: यहाँ बदलाव से अर्थ साफ़ होगा।

examples.en: A change here will make the meaning clear.

examples.t: शायद यह वाक्य छोटा किया जा सके।
examples.r: śāyad yah vākya chhoṭā kiyā jā sake.
examples.en: Perhaps this sentence could be shortened.

examples.t: मूल भाव बना रहे — स्वर न बदले।
examples.r: mūl bhāv banā rahe — svar na badle.
examples.en: Let the original sense survive — do not change the tone.

mistakes.wrong: यह वाक्य ग़लत है, ऐसे लिखिए।
mistakes.right: यहाँ बदलाव से अर्थ साफ़ होगा — ऐसा लिखें तो?
mistakes.why: यह ग़लत है comments on the writer; the suggestion form comments on the sentence. In an editorial round the difference decides whether the writer can receive the note.

dialogue.en: Shorten the second sentence — let the sense survive, only let the tone lighten.

lessons.title: Register matching, not word matching
lessons.learn: Translation chooses a register and keeps it. तत्सम words (आवश्यकता, सूचना, धन्यवाद) sit in formal text; तद्भव words (ज़रूरत, ख़बर, शुक्रिया) sit in speech. Putting one in the other's place is what makes a translation sound like a dictionary: the English is right word by word and wrong in the room.

grammar.title: One register, kept to the end
grammar.explain: The translator reads the source for its register first, then picks the Hindi layer and stays there — a नोटिस uses आवश्यकता and सूचित, a WhatsApp message uses ज़रूरत and बता देना. Mixed registers inside one paragraph are what reveal a translation; the grammar can be perfect and the text still reads wrong.
grammar.pattern: formal source → तत्सम layer · conversational source → तद्भव layer

lessons.title: Idioms, false friends and what not to translate
lessons.learn: Idioms move by sense, not by word: मुँह में पानी आना is 'to make one's mouth water', and word-for-word it is nonsense in English. False friends are quieter and more dangerous: नुक़सान is loss, not nuisance; मतलब is meaning, not motive; आराम is rest, not comfort as furniture.

grammar.title: Translate the भाव, not the शब्द
grammar.explain: An idiom is replaced by the target language's idiom, or by its plain sense if there is none: मुँह में पानी आना → to make one's mouth water. शब्दशः translation is kept only for glosses, never for the text itself. False friends are checked in संदर्भ (context) rather than in a dictionary, because a dictionary gives the commonest sense, not the sense in front of you.
grammar.pattern: idiom → target idiom · no target idiom → plain sense · check false friends in context

lessons.title: Back-translation as a check
lessons.learn: The professional check is back-translation: पहले अनुवाद, फिर पुनःअनुवाद (translate, then translate back), and compare the two Hindi texts. Where they diverge, the first translation has either added or dropped something — यहाँ कुछ जुड़ गया (here something has been added), यहाँ अर्थ घट गया (here the meaning has shrunk).

grammar.title: अनुवाद → पुनःअनुवाद → तुलना
grammar.explain: The method is mechanical, which is why it works: translate into Hindi, translate that Hindi back into English without looking at the source, then compare the two English texts. Extra information means the first pass explained too much (बारीक़ी जुड़ गई); lost information means it smoothed something over (अर्थ घट गया) — and smoothing is the commoner fault.

examples.r: yahāṅ kuchh juṛ gayā — mūl meṅ yah bāt nahīṅ hai.
examples.en: Something has been added here — this is not in the original.

examples.en: Here the meaning has shrunk — a fine detail was lost.

mistakes.why: a translation that reads smoothly is exactly the one that has quietly smoothed something away. The mechanical check catches what fluent reading hides.

lessons.title: Explaining a rule simply
lessons.learn: Teaching is the last test of understanding. A rule is explained with one example first, then the rule, then a second example: देखिए — मैं जाता हूँ, वह जाता है. नियम यह है कि क्रिया कर्ता के साथ बदलती है. The beginner's question is never 'why' but 'which one do I say', so the answer is an example, not a table.

grammar.title: Example → rule → example
grammar.explain: The teaching order is देखिए (look) → नियम यह है कि (the rule is) → अब आप कहिए (now you say it). Every rule is stated in one sentence with no jargon, and the learner's first attempt is answered with दोहराइए rather than a correction. क्रिया, कर्ता and कारक are taught only after the learner can use the thing.
grammar.pattern: देखिए … → नियम यह है कि … → अब आप कहिए …

examples.en: Look — I go, he goes.

examples.en: The rule is that the verb changes with the subject.

examples.en: Now you say it — “you go” (respectful).

mistakes.wrong: सबसे पहले कारक और विभक्ति समझिए।
mistakes.right: देखिए — यह वाक्य। अब आप ऐसा ही बनाइए।
mistakes.why: grammar terminology before usage teaches the learner to talk about the language instead of using it. Terms come after the learner has said the sentence correctly three times.

lessons.title: Correcting kindly
lessons.learn: Correction is delivered inside encouragement: बहुत अच्छा! बस एक चीज़ बदलिए (very good! just change one thing). Say the sentence back correctly rather than naming the mistake — कर्ता ग़लत है means nothing to a beginner, while saying the right sentence makes them hear it. ग़लती से सीखना (learning from the error) is the frame to give the learner.

grammar.title: प्रशंसा → सुधार → प्रशंसा

lessons.title: The first lesson, and the transliteration trap
lessons.learn: A first Hindi lesson teaches three things and no more: नमस्ते, मेरा नाम … है, and आप कैसे हैं?. The trap is transliteration — 'namaste' hides that there is no 't' as in English, and 'main' is not 'mine'. लिप्यंतरण (transliteration) helps for a week and then becomes a spelling habit; देवनागरी should arrive by week two.

grammar.title: Three sentences, then the script
grammar.explain: The first lesson's content is fixed: नमस्ते, मेरा नाम … है, आप कैसे हैं? — plus the answer मैं ठीक हूँ. Transliteration is a bridge with a date on it: it is used for a week and then replaced by देवनागरी, because the Roman spelling teaches the wrong vowels (main, namaste) and the wrong consonants (the retroflex ट/ड written as 't'/'d').
grammar.pattern: नमस्ते · मेरा नाम … है · आप कैसे हैं? → then देवनागरी

items.q: एक जगह बारीक़ी जुड़ गई, दूसरी जगह अर्थ घट गया। What were the two faults?

culture.text: Translation between Hindi and English has a direction problem. English into Hindi needs a register decision the source does not make for you — the same English sentence is आवश्यकता in a notice and ज़रूरत in a message. Hindi into English needs the opposite: the translator has to un-colloquialise, because spoken Hindi carries warmth (जी, अच्छा, ज़रा) that English flatly refuses to render, and losing it makes a warm speaker sound curt. Both directions are judged by the same test — whether the reader of the target text has the experience the reader of the source text had. That is why back-translation is taught here as a habit rather than a proofreading step.

reading.text: पिछले महीने मुझे एक सरकारी सूचना का अनुवाद करना पड़ा। सूचना में लिखा था: “समस्त आवेदकों को यथाशीघ्र आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ प्रस्तुत करने होंगे।” शब्दशः अनुवाद आसान था, पर वह किसी काम का नहीं था — अँग्रेज़ी पढ़ने वाले को वह वाक्य भारी लगता। पहले मैंने शैली चुनी: यह सूचना है, इसलिए कार्यालयीन परत। फिर मैंने लिखा: “All applicants must submit the required documents as soon as possible.” इसके बाद पुनःअनुवाद किया, और दो जगह अंतर मिला — एक जगह मैंने “ज़रूरी” जोड़ दिया था जो मूल में नहीं था। दूसरी जगह “समस्त” छूट गया था, जिससे अर्थ घट गया। दोनों सुधारकर मैंने फिर से लिखा। अब वह अनुवाद भरोसेमंद था, क्योंकि वह मूल जैसा व्यवहार करता था।
reading.gloss: Last month I had to translate a government notice. The notice said: “All applicants must submit the required documents as soon as possible.” A word-for-word translation was easy, but it was of no use — the English reader would find that sentence heavy. First I chose the register: this is a notice, so the official layer. Then I wrote: “All applicants must submit the required documents as soon as possible.” After that I back-translated, and found two differences — in one place I had added “necessary” which was not in the source. In the other, “all” had been dropped, which shrank the meaning. I corrected both and wrote it again. Now the translation was reliable, because it behaved like the original.

— सही कहा। और शुरू के दो पैराग्राफ़ बहुत भारी हैं — “समस्त प्रकार की व्यवस्थाओं का यथाशीघ्र क्रियान्वयन” जैसी भाषा।
— उसे छोटा कीजिए: “यह प्रक्रिया जल्दी लागू की जाएगी।”
— मूल भाव बना रहेगा?
— बना रहेगा — और पाठक पहले पैराग्राफ़ से ही समझ जाएगा।

— Then it is not a report, it is a description.

— Shorten it: “This procedure will be implemented soon.”
— Will the original sense survive?
— It will — and the reader will understand from the first paragraph itself.

mistakes.wrong: “मेरा मतलब साफ़ है” → “My motive is clear.”
mistakes.right: “मेरा मतलब साफ़ है” → “What I mean is clear.”
mistakes.why: मतलब is meaning; नीयत or इरादा is motive. The false friend is dangerous because the wrong sentence is perfectly fluent English.
ज़रूरत belongs to speech, आवश्यकता/आवश्यक to written official Hindi. The sentence is grammatical and still wrong — a register error, which is what C1+ is examined on.

mistakes.wrong: रिपोर्ट में सब कुछ है। (no summary, no recommendation)
mistakes.right: सारांश और सिफ़ारिश अलग से दीजिए।
mistakes.why: a report that requires reading from the start to find anything is a description. The summary and the recommendation are the parts that make it usable.

task.title: Translate, back-translate, then teach it
task.instructions: Take one paragraph of English — a notice, an email, a news paragraph — and do three things with it in Hindi: translate it choosing one register and staying in it; back-translate it without looking at the source and list every place the two differ, saying whether something was added or lost; then write four lines explaining to a beginner, in plain Hindi, the one rule your translation had to get right. The third step is the real test — if you cannot explain it simply, you made the choice by ear.
